We have template details. The mapped_rxn shows product on right side? Reaction: left side: Cl[CH2:10][Cl:11].[F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][cH:9][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1 >> product: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][c:9]([CH2:10][Cl:11])[cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

Thus product SMILES is the target molecule. We need to apply template to that product to get precursors. The precursors are the left side reactants: Cl[CH2:10][Cl:11] and [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][cH:9][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

We need to output list of lists of SMILES strings of precursors. So one combination: ["ClCCl"? Actually Cl[CH2][Cl] is dichloromethane? SMILES: ClCCl (Cl-CH2-Cl). That's "ClCCl". The other is the larger heterocycle with F substituent. Let's generate SMILES from mapped reaction: The second reactant SMILES: [F:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][cH:9][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

We need to convert to standard SMILES. Let's try to interpret: It's a bicyclic? Actually it's a 1,4-diazabicyclo? Let's just use the SMILES as given but remove atom mapping and brackets. Remove mapping numbers and brackets: [F] becomes F, [CH:2]1 becomes C1? Actually CH with aromatic? It's aliphatic CH. So "F C1 C C N(... ) C1". Let's reconstruct: F C1 C C N( C c2 c c c c c2 ) C1. The aromatic ring is c:6 with hydrogens. So it's a phenyl attached via CH2? The SMILES likely: "Fc1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1"? Wait need to map: [CH:2]1[CH2:3][N:4]([CH2:5][c:6]2[cH:7][cH:8][cH:9][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH2:14]1

Interpret: start ring: CH (position 2) with label 1, then CH2 (3) then N (4) then substituent CH2 (5) attached to aromatic carbon c6 which is part of a phenyl ring (c6 2 ...). Then after N, we have CH2 (14) then close ring to 1. So it's a 5-membered? Actually it's a piperidine? Let's try to write: F-CH-CH2-N(...)-CH2- (closing). So it's a fluorinated piperidine with phenyl substituent. The phenyl is attached via CH2 to N. So SMILES: "Fc1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1". That seems plausible: F attached to carbon of piperidine at position 1. The piperidine ring: C1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1. Yes that matches: F attached to C1. So the SMILES: "Fc1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1". Let's verify: The aromatic ring is phenyl (c2ccccc2). The CH2 linking to N is [CH2:5] attached to aromatic carbon c6. So N attached to CH2-phenyl. So N substituent is CH2-phenyl. So N has substituent CH2-phenyl and also part of ring. So N is tertiary. So final SMILES: "Fc1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1". That seems correct.

Thus precursors list: ["ClCCl", "Fc1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1"].

Return as list of list: [["ClCCl", "Fc1CCN(CCc2ccccc2)CC1"]].

Check if any other combinations? Template may produce only one set. So final answer.
